newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon minister seeks news on Red Army suspects.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon minister seeks news on Red Army suspects.

text.p: Lebanon's Justice Minister Bahij Tabbara has asked the prosecutor general for full a report on the case of Japanese Red Army suspects reported held in Lebanon, a newspaper reported on Friday.
"I have asked Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum to...inform me fully on this subject and I hope all the information will be ready by Saturday," Tabbara told the conservative Beirut daily an-Nahar.

The case has been mired in confusion since February 18 when Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in Tokyo that Lebanese officials had told him six Japanese Red Army suspects had been arrested in the eastern Bekaa Valley.

Lebanese officials have been tight-lipped since Hashimoto's statement, apart from Foreign Minister Faris Bouez who said publicly on the same day that arrests of Japanese Red Army members had taken place.

Confusion mounted this week when Interior Minister Michel al Murr and Lebanese security sources said no Lebanese security or military intelligence agency was holding any Japanese detainees. Judicial sources said they were sure that Syrian troops in Lebanon were not holding the Japanese.
